about: Who claims each contested area (plan 3.2, claims spec; docs/maps.md). Layer 1 is Natural Earth's, written by build/seed-claims.mjs: never edit it by hand. Each later layer is a review whose changes apply in order, each with a reason and a source.

layers.author: Natural Earth
layers.source: Natural Earth 5.1.2, admin-0 point-of-view fields (ADM0_A3 and ADM0_A3_xx), resolved to places by seed-claims.mjs

changes.reason: Dormant claim: Natural Earth's Taiwan view (ADM0_A3_TW) carries the Republic of China's constitutional claim to all of China, which the Taiwan government does not press. Only formal, current claims count (spec rule 2).
changes.source: Natural Earth 5.1.2 ADM0_A3_TW field; claims spec, plan.md 3.2 (2026-11-25)

changes.source: Natural Earth 5.1.2 geometry: SAH lies wholly inside B19 (91,000 of 269,000 km²)

changes.reason: Same shape as the Northern Cyprus map unit (spec rule 6).
changes.source: Natural Earth 5.1.2 geometry: B20 and CYN coincide

changes.reason: Same shape as the Somaliland map unit (spec rule 6).
changes.source: Natural Earth 5.1.2 geometry: B30 and SOL coincide

changes.reason: Ended: Azerbaijan retook the area in September 2023, the Republic of Artsakh dissolved itself from 1 January 2024, and Armenia recognises Azerbaijan's territorial integrity. No current claim against Azerbaijan remains.
changes.source: Republic of Artsakh presidential decree of 28 September 2023; Armenia–Azerbaijan peace agreement initialled in Washington, 8 August 2025

changes.reason: South Sudan claims Abyei as well as Sudan; its final status is undecided under the 2005 Abyei Protocol.
changes.source: UN Security Council resolution 2802 (14 November 2025), renewing UNISFA

changes.reason: Suriname claims the Tigri / New River Triangle, which Guyana administers; it protested Guyana's airstrip plans there in 2024 and restated the claim in 2026.
changes.source: Suriname Ministry of Foreign Affairs, summons of Guyana's ambassador (November 2024); Stabroek News, 30 November 2024

changes.reason: Suriname claims the Lawa headwaters between the Litani and Marouini rivers, which France administers as part of French Guiana.
changes.source: Suriname's official maps, which show the area within Suriname

changes.reason: The Philippines claims North Borneo (Sabah) in statute and restated the claim in 2026.
changes.source: Philippine Republic Act 5446 (1968), section 2; Department of Foreign Affairs statement, February 2026
